rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods <U+2013> two-year field experiments (2014, 2015) with maize in the North China Plain, RCB design, 12 treatments (lateral depths 0/15/30 cm, irrigation levels 70/100/130% ETc, sewage effluent vs groundwater), deep percolation and nitrate leaching monitored at 70 cm. Q2: Results 'Nitrate leaching' and Table 4 <U+2013> cumulative NO3<U+2013>N leaching at a given irrigation level generally increased as lateral depth increased; in 2014 lateral depth had a significant effect (P=0.062), I1D3 being 189 and 86% higher than I1D1 and I1D2; Table 5 and text <U+2013> sewage effluent irrigation gave generally higher cumulative NO3<U+2013>N leaching than groundwater (e.g., 54 vs 13 kg/ha at 15 cm depth in 2015); Conclusions 2. Q4: Results 'Deep percolation' and Table 4 <U+2013> deep percolation (tensiometer-derived flux at 70 cm) was generally higher for the 30 cm dripline (I3D3 78 and 13% higher than I3D1), explained by greater wetted depth; Table 6 and text <U+2013> NO3<U+2013>N concentration in leachate increased with lateral depth (23.2, 27.2, 36.2 mg/L for I1 D1<U+2013>D3 in 2015) attributed to nitrate accumulated in deeper soil; soil profile NO3<U+2013>N also measured. Q7: Results 'Nitrate leaching' <U+2013> authors state from their data that intensive rainfall was the driving force for NO3<U+2013>N leaching in the semi-humid region and that mobile NO3<U+2013>N content in soil was the principal factor for the quantity leached; most leaching occurred at the late growth stage with intensive rainfall. Q8: Results 'Nitrate leaching' <U+2013> authors note rainfall compensated for differences between treatments and that spatial variability of soil physical<U+2013>chemical properties could create variability in leachate concentration and deep percolation that dampens the influence of irrigation parameters on NO3<U+2013>N leaching; lateral-depth effect was significant only in 2014 and only at P=0.1; tensiometers installed in one replicate per treatment.
rows.notes: The study is on subsurface drip irrigation applying secondary sewage effluent (TSE), matching the passage. Q3 no: leaching estimated by a single method (tensiometer-derived Darcy flux times suction-cup concentration); soil N sampling was used only to interpret year differences, not to independently establish the lateral-depth effect. Q7 answered yes with some doubt: rainfall and mobile soil nitrate are stated as driving conditions for leaching generally rather than specifically as requirements for the lateral-depth effect. Q9 no: cumulative leaching values (Table 4) are single values per treatment with no dispersion; SDs in Table 6 refer to leachate concentration over time, not the leaching result; P-values only.

notes: Full text appears complete. Single site, single soil (silt loam), single crop (maize), two seasons; plot-scale experiment.
